sections.heading: Purpose of this letter
sections.text: This is a formal internal appeal of the denial dated September 5, 2026 for the emergency department visit and CT of the abdomen provided on August 14, 2026. The stated reason was that the provider is not in the plan's network and that the services were paid at the out-of-network rate. I ask Lone Star Benefit Solutions to overturn that decision and to reprocess the claim at the in-network cost-sharing level. This appeal is filed within the 180-day window allowed for internal appeals [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.filing_window]].

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text:
On August 14, 2026 I received emergency care from Gulf Coast Emergency Physicians, PLLC. The services billed were an emergency department visit, level 4 (CPT 99284) and a CT of the abdomen (CPT 74176). [ADD: briefly describe the symptoms that led you to seek emergency care.]

The explanation of benefits dated September 5, 2026 shows $4,800.00 billed, $1,321.60 paid by the plan, and $3,478.40 listed as my responsibility. The denial codes are PR-45 and N-661. The reason is quoted here exactly as written: "N-661: Provider is not in your plan's network. Services from a non-participating provider are paid at the out-of-network rate."

sections.heading: Why the claim should be reprocessed
sections.text:
This claim is for emergency services. Under the No Surprises Act, a plan must cover emergency care without prior authorization even when the treating provider is out of network, my cost sharing cannot be more than the in-network amount, and the provider cannot bill me for the balance [[cite:nsa.emergency.no_balance_billing]]. Paying the claim at the out-of-network rate and listing $3,478.40 as my responsibility does not match that protection [[cite:nsa.emergency.no_balance_billing]].

Emergency medicine, radiology, and diagnostic services are also among the specialties that cannot use a consent form to charge out-of-network rates, and consent cannot be used where the need was unforeseen and urgent [[cite:nsa.facility.no_consent_for_ancillary]]. [ADD: state whether you signed any consent or waiver form at the facility.]

Any cost sharing I do owe for these protected emergency services must be applied to my in-network deductible and in-network out-of-pocket maximum [[cite:nsa.emergency.counts_in_network]].

I will also supply a statement from the treating provider if the plan finds it helpful [ADD: name of treating provider, if you have it].

sections.heading: Requests
sections.text:
1. A complete copy of the claim file and every document, record, rule, guideline, or protocol relied on in deciding this claim, free of charge [[cite:fed.claim_file.free_copies]].

2. The specific plan provision and any internal criterion applied to this claim, together with the name and credentials of the person who made the decision [[cite:fed.notice.required_content]].

3. A written decision on this appeal within the time limit that applies to a post-service claim [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.decision_windows]].

4. Reprocessing of claim EOB-26-88120-4 at in-network cost sharing as protected emergency services, with the balance removed from my responsibility [[cite:nsa.emergency.no_balance_billing]].

5. Confirmation that any remaining cost sharing is credited to my in-network deductible and in-network out-of-pocket maximum [[cite:nsa.emergency.counts_in_network]].

6. A copy of any notice-and-consent form the plan believes applies to these services, or written confirmation that none exists [[cite:nsa.facility.no_consent_for_ancillary]].

I can be reached at [ADD: your phone number] or [ADD: your email address]. I reserve the right to request an independent external review after the plan's final internal decision [[cite:fed.external_review.filing_window]], and to raise this matter with the Texas Department of Insurance if the plan is one it regulates [[cite:tx.regulator.scope]] or with the federal No Surprises Help Desk [[cite:nsa.complaint.help_desk]].

Sincerely,

[ADD: your full name]
